summary: The authors design a control protocol for two-photon-dissipation-stabilized cat qubits using shortcut-to-adiabaticity inverse engineering within an effective two-level model of the cat subspace. motivation: Cat qubits promise hardware-efficient fault tolerance, but fast high-fidelity control that tolerates drive imperfections and avoids leakage is still needed.
method: They derive an effective two-level description of the dissipative cat subspace, inverse-engineer the control pulses, and analyse sensitivity to systematic control errors.
result: The protocol gives fast, high-fidelity state transfer with strongly reduced sensitivity to drive-amplitude errors, while two-photon dissipation suppresses leakage caused by pure dephasing (theory only; the abstract quotes no headline fidelity).
